title: Exercise Training-Increased FBXO32 and FOXO1 in a Gender-Dependent Manner in Mild Cognitively Impaired African Americans: GEMS-1 Study.
authors: Bedada, Fikru B; Ntekim, Oyonumo E; Nwulia, Evaristus O; Fungwe, Thomas V; Nadarajah, Sheeba Raaj; Obisesan, Thomas O
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过外周血基因表达分析探讨运动对轻度认知障碍非裔美国人中FBXO32和FOXO1表达的性别依赖性影响，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: The ubiquitin proteasome system (UPS) and FOXOs transcription factors play a pivotal role in cellular clearance and minimizing the accumulation of Abeta in neurodegeneration (ND). In African Americans (AAs) with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), the role of components of UPS and FOXOs; and whether they are amenable to exercise effects is unknown. We hypothesized that exercise can enhance cellular clearance systems during aging and ND by increasing expressions of FBXO32 and FOXO1. To test this hypothesis, we used TaqMan gene expression analysis in peripheral blood (PB) to investigate the component of UPS and FOXOs; and provide mechanistic insight at baseline, during exercise, and in both genders. At baseline, levels of FBXO32 were higher in women than in men. In our attempt to discern gender-specific exercise-related changes, we observed that levels of FBXO32 increased in men but not in women. Similarly, levels of FOXO1 increased in men only. These data suggest that a graded dose of FBXO32 and FOXO1 may be beneficial when PB cells carrying FBXO32 and FOXO1 summon into the brain in response to Alzheimer's disease (AD) perturbation (docking station PB cells). Our observation is consistent with emerging studies that exercise allows the trafficking of blood factors. Given the significance of FBXO32 and FOXO1 to ND and associated muscle integrity, our findings may explain, at least in part, the benefits of exercise on memory, associated gait, and balance perturbation acknowledged to herald the emergence of MCI.
abstract_zh: 泛素蛋白酶体系统（UPS）和FOXOs转录因子在细胞清除及减少神经退行性疾病（ND）中Abeta积累方面发挥关键作用。在患有轻度认知障碍（MCI）的非裔美国人（AAs）中，UPS和FOXOs各组分的角色及其是否受运动影响尚不清楚。我们假设运动可通过增加FBXO32和FOXO1的表达来增强衰老和ND过程中的细胞清除系统。为验证此假设，我们使用外周血（PB）中的TaqMan基因表达分析来研究UPS和FOXOs的组分，并在基线、运动期间及两性中提供机制性见解。在基线时，女性FBXO32水平高于男性。在尝试辨别性别特异性运动相关变化时，我们观察到男性FBXO32水平升高，而女性未出现此变化。同样，FOXO1水平仅在男性中升高。这些数据表明，当携带FBXO32和FOXO1的PB细胞响应阿尔茨海默病（AD）扰动（停靠站PB细胞）而被召集至大脑时，FBXO32和FOXO1的分级剂量可能有益。我们的观察与新兴研究一致，即运动允许血液因子运输。鉴于FBXO32和FOXO1对ND及相关肌肉完整性的重要性，我们的发现可能至少部分解释了运动对记忆、相关步态及平衡扰动（被认为是MCI出现的先兆）的益处。
